issues.title: [Bug]: `trap` around a query expression whose clause panics crashes the interpreter (Go index out of range)
issues.output:
error: runtime error: index out of range [18] with length 11
        at main(i1468.bal:6)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. Clean-context spec check: VALID. Integer division by zero panics (§6 multiplicative expr), the panic propagates out of the query (§6.35), and trap turns it into an error value (§6.34), so `true` is expected. Compilation succeeds and the crash happens while interpreting. --dump-bir shows the trap error-table entry [bb1,bb7] -> bb8 with result operand %1 (relative address in the function frame), but the query loop body does PushScopeFrame inside the trapped range. When the panic happens inside the scope frame, setRecoveredError (runtime/internal/exec/executor.go) resolves the relative operand against the inner scope frame, so no scope frames are unwound and bb8 runs in the inner frame -> index out of range. Classified backend (the executor does not restore the trap's frame depth); the fix might instead encode the depth in the error entry in birgen. Not frontend-crash (runtime crash). No duplicate found (#1168 is a different trap/lock issue).

issues.title: [Bug]: store to an object field through a wider object type is not checked, then fails with internal "unsupported type combination"
issues.output:
error: unsupported type combination: string + int64
        at main(i1469.bal:17)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. Clean-context spec check: VALID: C <: A by covariant field override; the store a.v = "x" must be checked at runtime against C's field type int and panic (§7 lvalues, impermissible store). Duplicate of open #1281 ('object field writes ignore the inherent field type', labelled runtime), whose reproducer (store nil through a wider object view) still exits 0 without a panic on current main: same missing runtime store check on object fields. The internal 'unsupported type combination' error is a downstream symptom of the same bug. Suggest closing as duplicate of #1281 (optionally add this reproducer there).
issues.close_reason: Duplicate of #1281: object field stores through a wider object type are not checked against the field's inherent type.

issues.title: [Bug]: computed-name field in a mapping constructor does not override a specific field with the same name (ignored or panics "duplicate key")
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. Clean-context spec check (fetched §6.7.2): all three expectations VALID: the mapping is first built without computed-name fields, then computed fields modify members in order, so the computed value wins and there is no duplicate-key panic. The 'duplicate key' panic is raised by the interpreter (runtime/internal/exec/non_terminators.go:58) and the computed-first case simply applies fields in source order, so this is backend. Related but not duplicate: #987 (computed key retypes the key variable), #856 (spread/shorthand fields).

issues.title: [Bug]: `value:fromJsonWithType` does not convert a JSON string to `xml` (inverse of `toJson`)
issues.output: true error {ballerina/lang.value}ConversionError ("'\"hi\"' value cannot be converted to 'xml'",message="'\"hi\"' value cannot be converted to 'xml'")
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. Clean-context spec check: VALID: fromJsonWithType does the inverse of toJson, which converts xml to a string via toString, so a JSON string must be parsed to xml when the target type is xml. lang.value function -> langlib. Related but not duplicate: #1026 (fromJsonWithType ignores record defaults), #657.

issues.title: [Bug]: record field default referring to its own type reports an invalid cycle
issues.output:
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: invalid cycle detected for type definition B
 --> i1475.bal:3:1
(the `type A B|int;` variant now reports the same diagnostic instead of the nil-pointer panic mentioned in the issue)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main (both variants). Clean-context spec check: VALID: a field default is an expression evaluated at construction, not part of the type's shape, so `is B` inside B's default is not a type-definition cycle; expected output {"x":1,"y":false}. Front end rejects a valid program -> frontend. Not frontend-crash: on current main both variants produce a SEMANTIC_ERROR diagnostic (the union-case panic in the issue no longer occurs). Related to #1325 (record default whose type refers back to the enclosing record; different symptom) but not a duplicate.

issues.title: [Bug]: module variable initialization cycle through a function parameter default is not detected
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: compiles and prints 0, i.e. reads g before it is initialized. Clean-context spec check: BUG: g depends on f via the call and f's default reads g, so there is no valid initialization order; reading an uninitialized variable is never defined, and it is inconsistent with the existing check for `int a = b; int b = a;`. (The issue itself notes the 2024R1 spec has no explicit rule; either way printing 0 is wrong.) Front-end dependency analysis -> frontend. Same root cause as open #1282 (initializer dependency analysis does not follow called functions' globals); suggested as parent_issue since a fix that follows calls would cover both.

issues.title: [Bug]: parameter defaults of isolated dependently-typed functions are not checked for isolation
issues.output: (compiles and runs, no output; the same default on a non-dependently-typed `isolated function h(int y = next())` gives error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: invocation of a non-isolated function)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. Clean-context spec check: INVALID-PROGRAM expected, i.e. the issue is valid: defaults of an isolated function must satisfy the isolated-function rules, so calling non-isolated next() there is a compile error; external body / dependent typing doesn't exempt it. Missing semantic check -> frontend. No duplicate found.
